news.headline: Irving contributed 11 points (5-19 FG, 1-8 3Pt), six assists, five rebounds, one block and one steal across 34 minutes during Tuesday's 120-101 win over the Nuggets.
news.story: Irving struggled mightily with efficiency but was still productive as a facilitator, finishing second on the Mavericks in assists while committing only one turnover. The veteran floor general has dished out at least five dimes in four of his last five games, averaging 20.6 points, 5.6 assists, 4.8 rebounds and 1.4 steals across 32.4 minutes per contest during that time.

news.headline: Irving had 16 points (6-13 FG, 4-8 3Pt), one rebound, eight assists and one steal in 27 minutes during Sunday's 116-114 victory over the Jazz.
news.story: Irving scored all 16 of his points in the first half, making his contributions as a facilitator particularly important as Dallas nearly surrendered an 18-point fourth-quarter lead and ended up grinding out a win. His combination of perimeter shooting and playmaking remains valuable, though his scoring output was modest after looking dominant in the first half. Still, Irving has now scored at least 16 points in four straight games and in seven of his nine appearances this month.

news.headline: Irving supplied 17 points (7-15 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, five assists and two steals over 29 minutes during Wednesday's 116-94 win over Golden State.
news.story: After sitting out the second game of a weekend back-to-back set, Irving returned to action and delivered decent numbers. The veteran point guard has scored in double digits in all 12 of his games this season, and he's contributed at least five boards and five assists in three of his seven November contests, averaging 22.9 points, 4.1 assists, 3.9 rebounds, 3.4 threes and 1.4 steals.

news.story: VanVleet has averaged 14.2 points, 5.6 assists and 2.6 three-pointers in 30.2 minutes over his last five appearances. Despite the scoring inconsistency, his established starting role and contributions in assists and triples sustain his fantasy value.

news.headline: VanVleet contributed 25 points (10-21 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 2-5 FT), one rebound, nine assists and one steal in 33 minutes during Friday's 133-124 loss to the Nuggets.
news.story: VanVleet posted a season high in scoring and nearly finished with a double-double. He also banked in a 51-foot three-pointer at the final buzzer, though it came far too late to matter. The veteran point guard has steadily found his rhythm over the past week.

news.headline: VanVleet finished Wednesday's 119-104 victory over Indiana with 15 points (6-13 FG, 3-7 3Pt), six assists, two rebounds and one steal over 27 minutes.
news.story: It was a solid bounce-back performance for VanVleet after the veteran point guard posted only eight points during Monday's loss to the Heat. He has recorded at least six assists in two of his last three outings and six times this season. VanVleet is averaging 14.0 points, 4.9 assists, 2.5 rebounds, 3.1 threes and 0.8 steals over 29.2 minutes per game in November.

news.story: This was Flagg's sixth double-double of the season, and his fourth game with one or fewer turnovers. It was also his 45th career 20-point game, moving him past Kevin Durant for the third-most 20-point games by a teenager in NBA history.

news.headline: Lendeborg is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Kings due to an illness.

news.headline: Porter finished with 11 points (4-8 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-3 FT), two rebounds, three assists and two steals across 15 minutes in Friday's 128-127 preseason overtime win over Indiana.

The 2019 No. 30 overall pick had a quality 2025-26 campaign from a statistical standpoint, averaging 17.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, 7.4 assists and 2.2 steals over 33.2 minutes per outing. It's been a rough season for the veteran big man, with Gobert averaging 7.6 points, 10.9 rebounds and 1.1 blocks while shooting 47.8 percent from the field and 46.2 percent from the line. However, it does appear as though his role is safe, which provides fantasy managers with a relatively safe floor, assuming blocks and rebounds are high on the priority list.

news.story: Burries was Milwaukee's most productive reserve and finished with a game-high plus-20 rating, providing an impressive display of his all-around potential. The rookie played seven more minutes than starting guard Ryan Rollins, and Burries' ability to contribute without needing considerable shot volume should help him carve out a meaningful role alongside Tyler Herro. Burries is worth monitoring in deeper fantasy formats, particularly if he continues receiving close to 30 minutes per contest.

news.headline: Burries ended with 26 points (12-20 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 0-1 FT), eight rebounds, four assists and one block over 26 minutes off the bench during Saturday's 132-129 loss to the 76ers.
news.story: The 26 points were a career high for the rookie guard, but Burries' big afternoon got overshadowed by Tyler Herro's career-high 50. This was Burries' first game with the second unit since Oct. 31, as Ryan Rollins moved back into the starting five, but the duo saw nearly equal workloads. Coach Taylor Jenkins might continue to mix and match next to Herro in his backcourt as he searches for a lineup that clicks.

news.story: Bassey finished one rebound shy of a double-double and missed just one of his seven field-goal attempts, but his contributions didn't end there. He also set season highs in assists and steals, making him one of Golden State's best players in this tight win. His long-term consistency will depend on maintaining a meaningful role in the Warriors' frontcourt rotation, though.

news.headline: Bassey ended with 16 points (6-7 FG, 4-5 FT), 13 rebounds, one assist, two blocks and one steal across 25 minutes during Thursday's 126-98 loss to the Grizzlies.
news.story: Bassey delivered his strongest performance of the season, capitalizing on increased minutes with his first double-double. He's started to establish a larger frontcourt role, combining efficient interior finishing with rebounding and rim protection. His limited offensive involvement caps his ceiling, but consistent minutes could make him a useful category-league streamer.

news.headline: Carter provided nine points (3-10 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 13 rebounds, three steals and two assists across 38 minutes during Tuesday's 104-86 loss to Detroit.
news.story: Carter narrowly missed out on a double-double, though his 13 rebounds led all players and matched his season-best mark. Tuesday's effort snapped a six-game stretch in which the big man recorded single-digit rebounds. On the year, Carter is averaging 12.5 points, 8.8 rebounds and 1.4 assists through 17 appearances.

news.headline: Carter amassed 15 points (5-11 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and one block in 32 minutes during Wednesday's 121-116 loss to Philadelphia.
news.story: Carter has scored in double figures in three consecutive games, averaging 12.3 points and 6.3 rebounds during that stretch. The veteran center has also connected on multiple three-pointers for the first time in November, providing an additional dimension to his offensive production. With Paolo Banchero (ankle) sidelined, Carter should continue seeing consistent minutes in Orlando's frontcourt, offering steady fantasy value in points and rebounds.

news.story: Ingram struggled with his shooting touch again, but that's to be expected after missing the first 15 regular-season outings. news.story: Ingram has been cleared to make his 2026-27 season debut after recovering from a partially torn Achilles, and he'll do so as a member of the first unit. He'll presumably have his minutes monitored closely Monday, though the team hasn't shared how large of a workload he'll take on in his team debut.

news.headline: Williams amassed 13 points (4-8 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, one assist and three steals in 25 minutes during Wednesday's 113-106 loss to the Timberwolves.
news.story: Williams followed his season-best scoring game Monday at Indiana with another productive night off the bench. He also tied his season high in steals. The veteran forward has quietly been one of the Thunder's most accurate three-point shooters, connecting at better than 40 percent. Oklahoma City's injuries have opened more minutes for him, and he's taking advantage.

news.headline: Williams finished with 20 points (8-13 FG, 4-6 3Pt), nine rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal across 26 minutes during Monday's 125-120 loss to Indiana.
news.story: Williams dropped a season-high 20 points, while also falling just one rebound short of what would have been his first double-double of the season. A plethora of injuries in Oklahoma City have presented Williams with an unexpected opportunity. While his numbers don't jump off the page, he is doing enough to be considered, even in standard leagues. In eight appearances over the past two weeks, he is averaging 10.0 points, 4.1 rebounds, 1.4 steals and 1.5 three-pointers, good enough for top-90 value during that span.

news.headline: Brown will start Monday's game against the Timberwolves, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
news.story: Brown has scored 15 and 18 points in his previous two showings, earning him the opportunity to join the starting five for the first time in his young NBA career. Coach Jordi Fernandez noted that Brown has been given the green light to log starter minutes, which would seemingly indicate that he'll sit around the 25-to-30-minute range Monday, though more clarity on his workload will be gleaned from how much he plays against the Timberwolves.

news.story: Brown bounced back from consecutive single-digit scoring efforts, benefiting from increased playing time and shot volume. However, his five turnovers highlighted the growing pains of handling significant offensive responsibility. His three-point shooting provides upside, but poor efficiency and limited defensive production make him a better dynasty stash than a standard-league option.

news.headline: Simons recorded three points (1-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT) in 18 minutes during Monday's 128-111 loss to Portland.
news.story: Simons had scored 18 points in consecutive appearances before Monday's dud. He's averaging 12.0 points and 1.8 three-pointers in 24.6 minutes over his last five games, but his fluctuating workload makes him difficult to trust in standard leagues.

news.headline: Simons racked up 18 points (6-13 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and one assist in 26 minutes off the bench during Saturday's 132-129 win over the Bucks.
news.story: After starting his first game of the season Wednesday while Tyrese Maxey dealt with a minor foot injury, Simons shifted back to the second unit and delivered at least 12 points for the fifth time in the last six games. The 27-year-old guard appears to be finding a groove with his new team after signing a two-year deal with the Sixers in July, averaging 15.2 points, 2.8 threes, 1.5 boards and 1.2 assists in 24.3 minutes while shooting 44.7 percent (17-for-38) from beyond the arc.

news.headline: Simons is not in the 76ers' starting lineup against the Bucks on Saturday, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
news.story: Tyrese Maxey (foot) has been cleared to return from a one-game absence, so Simons -- who made his first start of the season Wednesday against the Magic -- will revert to the bench for Saturday's contest. Simons has averaged 14.6 points per game while connecting on 56.9 percent of his field-goal attempts over his last five outings, and although he's back to a reserve role, he should still see plenty of opportunities on offense in the continued absence of Jaylen Brown (hamstring).

news.headline: Head coach Micah Nori said Morant met with a doctor in Los Angeles, who gave him a positive outlook on his recovery from the hamstring injury. While Nori declined to update Morant's timetable, he added Morant "may not be out for as long as we thought," Trail Blazers Insider Sean Highkin reports.
news.story: Morant was initially given a four-week timetable after he suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain on Oct. 30. It sounds like he's making solid progress, though it would be surprising to see him beat that timetable given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries. Scoot Henderson will continue to start in his absence, and there will be more minutes available for Jrue Holiday.

His five fouls Thursday restricted his playing time, but four offensive boards reinforced his interior impact. With 12 blocks over his last five appearances, he remains valuable in category leagues.

news.headline: VanVleet finished Wednesday's 119-104 victory over Indiana with 15 points (6-13 FG, 3-7 3Pt), six assists, two rebounds and one steal over 27 minutes.
news.story: It was a solid bounce-back performance for VanVleet after the veteran point guard posted only eight points during Monday's loss to the Heat. VanVleet is averaging 14.0 points, 4.9 assists, 2.5 rebounds, 3.1 threes and 0.8 steals over 29.2 minutes per game in November.

news.headline: Porter is signing a two-year contract with the Magic, Shams Charania of ESPN reports Wednesday.
news.story: Porter was waived by the Bucks following the preseason, though he's now set to provide backcourt depth for the Magic. He could challenge Jevon Carter for minutes behind Jalen Suggs right away. Over 38 regular-season appearances (36 starts) for Milwaukee last season, Porter averaged 17.4 points, 7.4 assists, 5.2 rebounds and 2.2 steals in 33.2 minutes per showing.

news.headline: Porter was waived by the Bucks on Monday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
news.story: Porter will need to search for an opportunity elsewhere after failing to secure a place on the regular-season roster. He averaged 17.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, 7.4 assists and 2.2 steals in 38 regular-season appearances a year ago with Milwaukee.

news.headline: Porter finished with 11 points (4-8 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-3 FT), two rebounds, three assists and two steals across 15 minutes in Friday's 128-127 preseason overtime win over Indiana.
news.story: While Porter had four turnovers, he was active on both sides of the floor to help the Bucks earn the win. The 2019 No. 30 overall pick had a quality 2025-26 campaign from a statistical standpoint, averaging 17.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, 7.4 assists and 2.2 steals over 33.2 minutes per outing. However, he was limited to 38 regular-season games. Porter is currently projected to come off the bench in 2026-27, though a decrease in minutes may actually help him stay healthy throughout the season.

news.headline: Irving contributed 11 points (5-19 FG, 1-8 3Pt), six assists, five rebounds, one block and one steal across 34 minutes during Tuesday's 120-101 win over the Nuggets.
news.story: Irving struggled mightily with efficiency but was still productive as a facilitator, finishing second on the Mavericks in assists while committing only one turnover. The veteran floor general has dished out at least five dimes in four of his last five games, averaging 20.6 points, 5.6 assists, 4.8 rebounds and 1.4 steals across 32.4 minutes per contest during that time.

news.headline: Irving had 16 points (6-13 FG, 4-8 3Pt), one rebound, eight assists and one steal in 27 minutes during Sunday's 116-114 victory over the Jazz.
news.story: Irving scored all 16 of his points in the first half, making his contributions as a facilitator particularly important as Dallas nearly surrendered an 18-point fourth-quarter lead and ended up grinding out a win. His combination of perimeter shooting and playmaking remains valuable, though his scoring output was modest after looking dominant in the first half. Still, Irving has now scored at least 16 points in four straight games and in seven of his nine appearances this month.

news.headline: Irving supplied 17 points (7-15 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, five assists and two steals over 29 minutes during Wednesday's 116-94 win over Golden State.
news.story: After sitting out the second game of a weekend back-to-back set, Irving returned to action and delivered decent numbers. The veteran point guard has scored in double digits in all 12 of his games this season, and he's contributed at least five boards and five assists in three of his seven November contests, averaging 22.9 points, 4.1 assists, 3.9 rebounds, 3.4 threes and 1.4 steals.

news.headline: Gobert ended Wednesday's 113-106 victory over the Thunder with nine points (4-6 FG, 1-6 FT), seven rebounds and one steal across 32 minutes.
news.story: Gobert was efficient, but struggled again at the free-throw line, a problem that has followed him all season. The center is still averaging double-digit rebounds, and Minnesota has learned to live with his shaky foul shooting because of what he brings defensively.

news.headline: Gobert accumulated seven points (2-2 FG, 3-4 FT), 11 rebounds, two assists, three blocks and one steal over 32 minutes during Saturday's 104-95 victory over the Grizzlies.
news.story: Gobert started to turn things around Saturday, blocking at least three shots for just the second time this season. It's been a rough season for the veteran big man, with Gobert averaging 7.6 points, 10.9 rebounds and 1.1 blocks while shooting 47.8 percent from the field and 46.2 percent from the line. However, it does appear as though his role is safe, which provides fantasy managers with a relatively safe floor, assuming blocks and rebounds are high on the priority list.

news.headline: Gobert posted nine points (4-6 FG, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds and two steals over 35 minutes during Thursday's 102-99 loss to the Knicks.
news.story: Gobert has grabbed seven or fewer rebounds in three of his last four games, an unusual slump for the veteran center. His 35-minute workload is encouraging, but inconsistent rebounding and shot-blocking have diminished his fantasy impact.

news.headline: Young chipped in 17 points (4-9 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 8-9 FT), 12 assists and two steals across 35 minutes during Tuesday's 131-116 loss to Boston.
news.story: Young attempted fewer than 10 field goals despite playing 35 minutes, and he's been shifting into more of a playmaking role than a scoring one, as he's attempted 10 or fewer shots in five of his last six appearances. With Anthony Davis, Kyshawn George and AJ Dybantsa capable of handling considerable scoring responsibilities, Young doesn't necessarily need to deliver explosive scoring performances to remain an elite source of fantasy production in assists. He's averaged 15.4 points, 8.4 assists, 2.2 rebounds and 1.5 steals per game since the beginning of November.

news.story: Young has shot just 26 percent over his last five games, averaging 31 minutes. However, he's recorded at least eight assists in four of those contests, maintaining fantasy value through playmaking. His shooting struggles remain concerning, but his established offensive role provides upside.

news.headline: Lendeborg supplied 15 points (6-11 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), eight rebounds, two assists, one block and three steals over 31 minutes during Wednesday's 129-110 win over the Kings.

Through 12 games on the month, Lendeborg is averaging 18.6 points, 7.2 boards, 3.7 assists, 1.8 threes, 1.3 steals and 0.9 blocks, failing to score in double digits just once in that span.

news.headline: Lendeborg (illness) is available for Wednesday's game against the Kings, Luca Evans of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
news.story: Lendeborg was questionable to suit up due to an illness, but he went through pregame warmups and will give it a go versus Sacramento. Across 17 regular-season outings (all starts), he's averaging 19.2 points, 7.4 rebounds, 3.6 assists, 1.0 steals, 0.8 blocks and 1.9 three-pointers in 31.8 minutes.

news.headline: Lendeborg is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Kings due to an illness.
news.story: The standout rookie is in danger of sitting out for the first time all season. Georges Niang and Gui Santos would be in line for more playing time in the frontcourt if Lendeborg isn't feeling well enough to play.

news.story: Fox sat out Monday's 123-107 win over Sacramento due to a right shin contusion, and he's now in danger of missing a second consecutive outing due to the injury. Stephon Castle will continue to see increased usage if Fox remains sidelined.

news.story: Morant was initially given a four-week timetable after he suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain on Oct. 30. It sounds like he's making solid progress, though it would be surprising to see him beat that timetable given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries. Scoot Henderson will continue to start in his absence, and there will be more minutes available for Jrue Holiday.

The star guard leaves a major void in the Trail Blazers' starting backcourt, one that figures to be filled by Jrue Holiday for the foreseeable future.

news.headline: Simons recorded three points (1-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT) in 18 minutes during Monday's 128-111 loss to Portland.
news.story: Simons had scored 18 points in consecutive appearances before Monday's dud. He's averaging 12.0 points and 1.8 three-pointers in 24.6 minutes over his last five games, but his fluctuating workload makes him difficult to trust in standard leagues.

news.headline: Simons racked up 18 points (6-13 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and one assist in 26 minutes off the bench during Saturday's 132-129 win over the Bucks.
news.story: After starting his first game of the season Wednesday while Tyrese Maxey dealt with a minor foot injury, Simons shifted back to the second unit and delivered at least 12 points for the fifth time in the last six games. The 27-year-old guard appears to be finding a groove with his new team after signing a two-year deal with the Sixers in July, averaging 15.2 points, 2.8 threes, 1.5 boards and 1.2 assists in 24.3 minutes while shooting 44.7 percent (17-for-38) from beyond the arc.

news.headline: Simons is not in the 76ers' starting lineup against the Bucks on Saturday, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
news.story: Tyrese Maxey (foot) has been cleared to return from a one-game absence, so Simons -- who made his first start of the season Wednesday against the Magic -- will revert to the bench for Saturday's contest. Simons has averaged 14.6 points per game while connecting on 56.9 percent of his field-goal attempts over his last five outings, and although he's back to a reserve role, he should still see plenty of opportunities on offense in the continued absence of Jaylen Brown (hamstring).

news.headline: Ingram registered 18 points (6-19 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds and four assists in 26 minutes during Wednesday's 115-97 loss to the Grizzlies.
news.story: Ingram struggled with his shooting touch again, but that's to be expected after missing the first 15 regular-season outings. In his two games since returning from a partially torn Achilles, Ingram is averaging 17.0 points, 6.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists in 26.5 minutes while shooting 32.4 percent (12-37 FG) from the field and 16.7 percent (2-12 3Pt) from behind the arc.

news.headline: Ingram provided 16 points (6-18 FG, 0-6 3Pt, 4-5 FT), seven rebounds and four assists in 27 minutes during Monday's 116-104 loss to Houston.
news.story: Ingram made his season debut and first appearance for the Clippers after undergoing surgery on his heel and partially torn Achilles tendon. While the former All-Star struggled from the field, his 18 shot attempts were encouraging given he hadn't played since May, and that paints a clear picture of the role he'll have as he gets back into game shape. news.story: Ingram has been cleared to make his 2026-27 season debut after recovering from a partially torn Achilles, and he'll do so as a member of the first unit. He'll presumably have his minutes monitored closely Monday, though the team hasn't shared how large of a workload he'll take on in his team debut.

news.story: Burries was Milwaukee's most productive reserve and finished with a game-high plus-20 rating, providing an impressive display of his all-around potential. The rookie played seven more minutes than starting guard Ryan Rollins, and Burries' ability to contribute without needing considerable shot volume should help him carve out a meaningful role alongside Tyler Herro. Burries is worth monitoring in deeper fantasy formats, particularly if he continues receiving close to 30 minutes per contest.

news.headline: Burries ended with 26 points (12-20 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 0-1 FT), eight rebounds, four assists and one block over 26 minutes off the bench during Saturday's 132-129 loss to the 76ers.
news.story: The 26 points were a career high for the rookie guard, but Burries' big afternoon got overshadowed by Tyler Herro's career-high 50. This was Burries' first game with the second unit since Oct. 31, as Ryan Rollins moved back into the starting five, but the duo saw nearly equal workloads. Coach Taylor Jenkins might continue to mix and match next to Herro in his backcourt as he searches for a lineup that clicks.

news.story: Bassey finished one rebound shy of a double-double and missed just one of his seven field-goal attempts, but his contributions didn't end there. He also set season highs in assists and steals, making him one of Golden State's best players in this tight win. His long-term consistency will depend on maintaining a meaningful role in the Warriors' frontcourt rotation, though.

news.headline: Bassey ended with 16 points (6-7 FG, 4-5 FT), 13 rebounds, one assist, two blocks and one steal across 25 minutes during Thursday's 126-98 loss to the Grizzlies.
news.story: Bassey delivered his strongest performance of the season, capitalizing on increased minutes with his first double-double. He's started to establish a larger frontcourt role, combining efficient interior finishing with rebounding and rim protection. His limited offensive involvement caps his ceiling, but consistent minutes could make him a useful category-league streamer.

news.headline: Brunson finished with 19 points (6-22 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 5-6 FT), three rebounds and five assists over 36 minutes during Wednesday's 121-102 victory over the Cavaliers.
news.story: Brunson had his worst shooting night of the season, but the Knicks didn't need him to be at his best. He still found ways to contribute as a playmaker, and the Knicks kept their winning streak going. With OG Anunoby (calf) out, he remains the clear focal point of a team that has climbed to 12-6.

news.headline: Brunson (illness) is available for Wednesday's game against the Cavaliers, Ian Begley of SportsNet New York reports.
news.story: Brunson popped on the injury report due to an illness but will avoid his first absence of the 2026-27 campaign. In two meetings with Cleveland this season, the 30-year-old is averaging 29.0 points, 4.5 rebounds and 7.0 assists while shooting 40.0 percent from deep over 34.5 minutes per contest.

news.headline: Brunson (illness) is probable for Wednesday's game against Cleveland.
news.story: Brunson is under the weather but is expected to play through the ailment. The superstar floor general is looking to extend his streak of 20-point, five-assist performances to eight Wednesday.

news.story: Williams followed his season-best scoring game Monday at Indiana with another productive night off the bench. He also tied his season high in steals. The veteran forward has quietly been one of the Thunder's most accurate three-point shooters, connecting at better than 40 percent. Oklahoma City's injuries have opened more minutes for him, and he's taking advantage.

news.headline: Williams finished with 20 points (8-13 FG, 4-6 3Pt), nine rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal across 26 minutes during Monday's 125-120 loss to Indiana.
news.story: Williams dropped a season-high 20 points, while also falling just one rebound short of what would have been his first double-double of the season. A plethora of injuries in Oklahoma City have presented Williams with an unexpected opportunity. While his numbers don't jump off the page, he is doing enough to be considered, even in standard leagues. In eight appearances over the past two weeks, he is averaging 10.0 points, 4.1 rebounds, 1.4 steals and 1.5 three-pointers, good enough for top-90 value during that span.

news.headline: James ended with 25 points (9-15 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 3-3 FT), 10 rebounds, 12 assists and one steal across 35 minutes in Wednesday's 111-104 win over Miami.
news.story: With Joel Embiid (illness) ruled out and Jaylen Brown (hamstring) exiting the game, James took over. He finished with his 126th career triple-double and first as a member of the 76ers. The 41-year-old is now averaging 17.1 points, 6.9 rebounds, 6.9 assists and 1.1 steals over 32.7 minutes per contest in 15 regular-season appearances in 2026-27. James isn't nearly as productive as he once was, though he should remain a reliable contributor for Philadelphia, assuming he stays off the injury report.

However, his five turnovers highlighted the growing pains of handling significant offensive responsibility. His three-point shooting provides upside, but poor efficiency and limited defensive production make him a better dynasty stash than a standard-league option.

news.story: Hunter erupted for a season high, easily topping his previous best and knocking down nearly everything he threw up. His layup with under two minutes left tied the game, though the Kings couldn't hold on. It was a big bounce-back after a rough shooting night against Phoenix on Wednesday.

Despite inconsistent shooting, Walter's perimeter volume is encouraging, as he has attempted six or more three-pointers in each of his last nine contests. More encouraging was his versatility Wednesday, as he also recorded seven rebounds, six assists and three steals while playing a substantial role in Toronto's depleted rotation. news.story: Walter erupted with a season high in scoring while setting a new career best with seven three-pointers. The third-year guard rebounded from a tough two-game stretch in which he shot a combined 4-for-16 (25 percent) from the field and 2-for-12 (16.7 percent) from behind the arc. Walter's performance wasn't enough to keep Toronto from losing a fifth straight game, as the Knicks have now beaten the Raptors 15 consecutive times, per Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca. news.headline: McDaniels finished with 32 points (11-15 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 6-6 FT), 10 rebounds, five assists, one steal and one block across 37 minutes in Wednesday's 113-106 win over Oklahoma City.
news.story: McDaniels scored a career-high 34 points in Monday's win over Brooklyn, and he narrowly missed that mark Wednesday. It's been a stellar 2026-27 campaign overall for the 26-year-old, who is now averaging 19.2 points, 6.4 rebounds and 3.8 assists, all career bests, along with 1.2 steals over 34.1 minutes in 19 regular-season appearances. With Anthony Edwards (knee) sidelined and LaMelo Ball (ankle) exiting the meeting with the Thunder, McDaniels could continue to play at an All-Star level for the foreseeable future.

news.story: Davion Mitchell is turning heads and leading the league in assists, Quentin Grimes is on a heater in Los Angeles and Cedric Coward is quickly emerging as a fantasy force. All are moving up the fantasy rankings. Meanwhile, Kel'el Ware's stint for the 1-16 Bucks has been a nightmare, Jalen Green is not pulling his weight in Phoenix and De'Aaron Fox has really struggled in San Antonio. news.headline: Porter is signing a two-year contract with the Magic, Shams Charania of ESPN reports Wednesday.
news.story: Porter was waived by the Bucks following the preseason, though he's now set to provide backcourt depth for the Magic. He could challenge Jevon Carter for minutes behind Jalen Suggs right away. Over 38 regular-season appearances (36 starts) for Milwaukee last season, Porter averaged 17.4 points, 7.4 assists, 5.2 rebounds and 2.2 steals in 33.2 minutes per showing.

news.headline: Porter was waived by the Bucks on Monday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
news.story: Porter will need to search for an opportunity elsewhere after failing to secure a place on the regular-season roster. He averaged 17.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, 7.4 assists and 2.2 steals in 38 regular-season appearances a year ago with Milwaukee.

news.headline: Porter finished with 11 points (4-8 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-3 FT), two rebounds, three assists and two steals across 15 minutes in Friday's 128-127 preseason overtime win over Indiana.
news.story: While Porter had four turnovers, he was active on both sides of the floor to help the Bucks earn the win. The 2019 No. 30 overall pick had a quality 2025-26 campaign from a statistical standpoint, averaging 17.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, 7.4 assists and 2.2 steals over 33.2 minutes per outing. However, he was limited to 38 regular-season games. Porter is currently projected to come off the bench in 2026-27, though a decrease in minutes may actually help him stay healthy throughout the season.

news.headline: George supplied 15 points (4-9 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 5-5 FT), five rebounds and seven assists over 26 minutes during Sunday's 116-114 loss to Dallas.
news.story: George provided balanced production despite playing fewer than 27 minutes, and while Utah's remarkable comeback was driven primarily by Svi Mykhailiuk's perimeter shooting, George still made his presence felt -- he was Utah's third-leading scorer and paced the team in assists. His role as a playmaker and scorer gives him a solid fantasy floor even in games in which his shooting volume isn't very high. His nine field-goal attempts Sunday were a season-low mark.

news.headline: George finished Friday's 111-101 loss to the Suns with 14 points (4-17 FG, 0-7 3Pt, 6-7 FT), three rebounds and six assists across 36 minutes.
news.story: George came crashing back to earth after back-to-back 30-point games against the two Los Angeles teams. He went cold from deep, and his late turnover ended any hope of a comeback. Off nights like this will happen with Lauri Markkanen (hand) out and defenses keying in on George. He is still averaging 21.6 points and 7.1 assists as Utah's go-to floor general.

news.headline: George supplied 30 points (9-17 FG, 5-10 3Pt, 7-9 FT), one rebound, 10 assists and one steal in 39 minutes during Wednesday's 109-97 victory over the Lakers.
news.story: George was instrumental in Utah's second consecutive upset, scoring nine points in the fourth quarter to help end Los Angeles' nine-game winning streak. His five three-pointers also matched his highest total of the season, and the 10 assists were the fourth time he has dished out double-digit dimes. With the Jazz continuing to lean on their younger players, George has considerable freedom to generate offense. news.story: Shamet made another start with OG Anunoby (calf) sidelined, supplying three triples and 17 points in an expanded role. Shamet's 15 field-goal attempts stood out, and the veteran is not afraid to let it fly when he has the chance. news.headline: Shamet will start in Saturday's game versus the Trail Blazers, James L. Edwards III of The Athletic reports.
news.story: The Knicks are down Karl-Anthony Towns (illness) and OG Anunoby (calf), so Shamet's services will be required in the starting lineup. The 29-year-old has started three times during the 2026-27 campaign, averaging 8.7 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.7 assists over 27.3 minutes per contest in those appearances.

news.headline: Shamet totaled 10 points (3-4 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two assists, one rebound and one steal in 30 minutes during Thursday's 102-99 victory over the Timberwolves.
news.story: Shamet turned in an efficient performance in limited shot attempts, leading the second unit in scoring. He's scored in double figures in three straight games, averaging 15.0 points, 1.3 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 28.0 minutes per showing over that stretch.

signals.detail: Brown made his first career start with Nolan Traore (hamstring) sidelined.

news.headline: Brown finished Monday's 142-116 loss to the Timberwolves with 17 points (6-12 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, seven assists and one steal over 29 minutes.
news.story: Brown made his first career start with Nolan Traore (hamstring) sidelined. The rookie has scored at least 15 points in three straight games and could gain considerable fantasy value if he maintains a starting role, though turnovers remain a concern.

news.headline: Brown will start Monday's game against the Timberwolves, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
news.story: Brown has scored 15 and 18 points in his previous two showings, earning him the opportunity to join the starting five for the first time in his young NBA career. Coach Jordi Fernandez noted that Brown has been given the green light to log starter minutes, which would seemingly indicate that he'll sit around the 25-to-30-minute range Monday, though more clarity on his workload will be gleaned from how much he plays against the Timberwolves.

news.headline: Brown registered 15 points (4-10 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 5-6 FT), one rebound and four assists over 27 minutes during Wednesday's 137-107 loss to the Bulls.
news.story: Brown bounced back from consecutive single-digit scoring efforts, benefiting from increased playing time and shot volume. However, his five turnovers highlighted the growing pains of handling significant offensive responsibility. His three-point shooting provides upside, but poor efficiency and limited defensive production make him a better dynasty stash than a standard-league option.

news.headline: Castle had 20 points (6-18 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 6-6 FT), six rebounds and nine assists across 34 minutes during Wednesday's 116-111 loss to the Trail Blazers.
news.story: The third-year guard just missed recording his fourth double-double of the season. Castle has scored 20-plus points in five of the last seven games, averaging 21.4 points, 8.6 assists, 4.9 boards, 2.9 threes and 1.1 steals over that stretch, and after producing five triple-doubles last season, it seems like it's just a matter of time until he collects his first of 2026-27.

news.headline: Castle produced 28 points (9-23 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 6-6 FT), eight rebounds and 11 assists in 37 minutes during Monday's 123-107 victory over the Kings.
news.story: Castle was forced into the spotlight Monday while the Spurs navigated without the services of De'Aaron Fox (shin), Dylan Harper (hip) and Victor Wembanyama (back), and he didn't disappoint. Castle looked sharp once again from downtown, where he's now hit at a clip of 54.2 percent from deep over his last four appearances. The 22-year-old also stepped up as a distributor and has secured a double-double in two of his last three showings.

news.headline: Castle posted 19 points (7-12 FG, 5-7 3Pt), three rebounds and six assists over 29 minutes during Saturday's 114-91 win over the Pelicans.
news.story: Castle finished as the Spurs' second-leading scorer behind Victor Wembanyama, who led the way with 50 points, and Castle was particularly deadly from beyond the arc. Four of his five three-pointers came during a third-quarter stretch that helped San Antonio pull away for good. Castle's ability to contribute as both a scorer and facilitator gives him multiple paths to fantasy value, while efficient perimeter shooting adds another dimension to his offensive profile.

news.story: Edgecombe continues to quietly go about his business, consistently producing on both ends of the floor. Through 18 appearances this season, he has averaged 13.9 points, 6.3 rebounds, 4.2 assists, 1.7 steals and 1.6 three-pointers, good enough for top-35 value in nine-category leagues. With Jaylen Brown (hamstring) likely to miss at least a couple of games, Edgecombe should see a small bump in usage, adding to his overall appeal.

news.story: Edgecombe continues to contribute across multiple categories despite inconsistent scoring. He's averaged 17.3 points, 6.0 rebounds, 6.3 assists and 2.0 steals over his last three appearances, while his substantial playing time provides a strong fantasy foundation.

news.headline: Wilson is undergoing surgery for a fractured right hand and will miss at least four to six weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
news.story: The rookie forward went down during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, and he now needs surgery to repair a fractured right hand. More pressure will likely fall on Josh Giddey and Matas Buzelis offensively going forward, while the likes of Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro will have a chance for added streaming value for the next month or so.

news.headline: Wilson won't return to Wednesday's game against the Spurs due to a right hand injury. He'll finish with 15 points (5-7 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds and one steal in 15 minutes.
news.story: Wilson turned in an efficient performance en route to 15 points before exiting Wednesday's contest early in the third quarter. The rookie forward's status will be worth monitoring ahead of Friday's game against Atlanta. If he's forced to miss time, Leonard Miller, Patrick Williams and Noa Essengue would be candidates for increased minutes.

news.headline: Wilson exited to the locker room in the third quarter of Wednesday's game against San Antonio due to an apparent hand injury, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.
news.story: Wilson was spotted holding his hand while heading back to the locker room. The rookie forward can be considered questionable to return until more information comes to light.

news.headline: Detroit recalled Duren (hamstring) from the G League's Motor City Cruise on Wednesday.
news.story: Duren has been dealing with a hamstring strain since October, and his return is not yet expected in immediate contests. The fact that he has practiced with the G League club is still a good sign as he makes progress in his recovery. Duren would be a reliable source of production once he's healthy, but until then, John Collins and Paul Reed may continue to absorb his responsibilities at center.

news.headline: Duren (hamstring) is being assigned to the Motor City Cruise on Wednesday for practice as he ramps up for a potential return, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports.
news.story: With Duren still out for Detroit but now progressing to a G League practice assignment, this marks a tangible step forward in his recovery from the right hamstring strain that has kept him sidelined since Oct. 23. The Pistons haven't provided a return timeline, but his return appears to be drawing closer as he increases his activity.

news.headline: Duren (hamstring) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Magic.
news.story: Duren hasn't played since Oct. 23 due to a right hamstring strain, though he's expected to be re-evaluated soon. Until the Pistons offer an update on the 23-year-old big man's progress, he can be considered week-to-week. Paul Reed will likely continue seeing increased minutes for as long as Duren is sidelined.

news.headline: Wiggins won't start Sunday's game against Detroit, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
news.story: Kingston Flemings (back) has been cleared to return to action, sending Wiggins back to the second unit. The 27-year-old forward has averaged 14.0 points, 3.6 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 2.8 three-pointers in 25.4 minutes per contest across his last five outings off the bench.

news.headline: Wiggins recorded 19 points (7-12 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three assists, two rebounds and one steal over 34 minutes in a 111-97 win over the Hornets on Friday.
news.story: Making his second start of the season, Wiggins scored 12 of his 19 points in the second half to finish as the Hawks' second-leading scorer behind Jalen Johnson (26). In his first season in Atlanta, Wiggins is averaging 14.3 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.4 assists, 0.9 steals and 2.9 threes over 26.1 minutes per game. He could revert to the bench against the Pistons on Sunday if rookie Kingston Flemings (back) is cleared to return for that contest.

news.headline: Wiggins will start Wednesday's game against Oklahoma City, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
news.story: With CJ McCollum (calf) and Kingston Flemings (back) ruled out, Wiggins will start for the first time this season. The 27-year-old started 21 regular-season games in 2025-26, averaging 13.6 points, 4.6 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.6 steals over 29.0 minutes per outing in those appearances.

news.headline: Nembhard produced 16 points (5-13 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 4-7 FT), two rebounds and eight assists in 32 minutes during Sunday's 113-106 loss to the Knicks.
news.story: Nembhard continued to handle significant ball-handling responsibilities for Indiana, producing eight assists while contributing 16 points. However, his six turnovers were costly and diminished an otherwise useful fantasy performance. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) unavailable, Nembhard's opportunities to facilitate the offense remain substantial, making his assist production an important component of his fantasy value. He has also scored in double digits in five straight appearances, averaging 13.8 points, 2.8 rebounds and 8.8 assists per game in that stretch.

news.headline: Nembhard (hip) is available for Friday's game against the Cavaliers, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
news.story: Nembhard missed the last two games while dealing with a hip issue. After initially carrying a questionable designation, he is good to go for Friday's meeting with the Cavs. As a result, Quenton Jackson is expected to head back to the bench.

news.headline: Nembhard (hip) is questionable for Friday's game in Cleveland.
news.story: Nembhard is battling a left hip injury. Head coach Rick Carlisle indicated that the 26-year-old wouldn't be out long, though it remains to be seen if he can get back on the floor Friday against the Cavaliers. If Nembhard misses a third consecutive contest, Quenton Jackson would presumably remain in the starting lineup.

news.headline: Lopez amassed three points (1-3 FG, 1-1 3Pt), four rebounds and one assist over 21 minutes during Monday's 116-104 loss to the Rockets.
news.story: Lopez delivered a disappointing performance, especially after having averaged 20.0 points per game over his previous five appearances. Isaiah Jackson and Yanic Konan Niederhauser combined for 26 minutes off the bench, and if that becomes a trend going forward, Lopez's fantasy upside will decrease quickly. He's valuable as a streaming option at center when he receives a fair share of playing time and offensive touches, but if that's not the case, his upside is fairly limited in other categories, especially the defensive ones.

news.story: White has averaged 16.6 points, 5.2 assists and 26.0 minutes over his last five appearances. His inconsistent shooting remains a concern, but his improving playing time and playmaking responsibilities help stabilize his fantasy value.

news.headline: White registered 21 points (7-18 FG, 5-10 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, two assists and one block over 28 minutes during Monday's 117-111 loss to Memphis.
news.story: White has scored at least 19 points in four of his last five appearances, averaging 18.6 points and 4.3 made three-pointers per game during that stretch. His growing workload and perimeter production strengthen his fantasy appeal.

news.headline: Jaquez totaled 21 points (9-15 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 2-4 FT), five rebounds, four assists and two steals across 34 minutes during Wednesday's 104-97 loss to Brooklyn.
news.story: Jaquez responded to a three-point outing Monday with his highest scoring total in five games. His playing time also jumped after four consecutive appearances under 30 minutes, offering encouragement for his fantasy outlook if the expanded role continues.

news.headline: Jaquez is in the Bucks' starting lineup against the 76ers on Saturday.
news.story: Jaquez has come off the bench for each of the Bucks' last five games, but he'll rejoin the starting five along with Ryan Rollins while Brayden Burries and Nate Ament move to bench roles. Jaquez started in each of Milwaukee's first 11 games of the regular season and averaged 15.3 points, 5.7 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.7 threes and 0.5 steals over 27.5 minutes per contest in that span.

news.headline: Jaquez finished Thursday's 124-114 loss to the Trail Blazers with nine points (3-11 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two assists, one rebound and one steal across 22 minutes.
news.story: Jaquez struggled with efficiency off the bench once again, and he's shot just 32.0 percent from the field over the last three games. The fourth-year swingman has scored single-digit points in two of those three outings, during which he's averaged 8.3 points, 3.7 assists, 2.7 rebounds and 1.0 steals across 25.0 minutes per contest.

news.headline: Williams amassed 13 points (4-8 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, one assist and three steals in 25 minutes during Wednesday's 113-106 loss to the Timberwolves.
news.story: Williams followed his season-best scoring game Monday at Indiana with another productive night off the bench. He also tied his season high in steals. The veteran forward has quietly been one of the Thunder's most accurate three-point shooters, connecting at better than 40 percent. Oklahoma City's injuries have opened more minutes for him, and he's taking advantage.

news.headline: Williams finished with 20 points (8-13 FG, 4-6 3Pt), nine rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal across 26 minutes during Monday's 125-120 loss to Indiana.
news.story: Williams dropped a season-high 20 points, while also falling just one rebound short of what would have been his first double-double of the season. A plethora of injuries in Oklahoma City have presented Williams with an unexpected opportunity. While his numbers don't jump off the page, he is doing enough to be considered, even in standard leagues. In eight appearances over the past two weeks, he is averaging 10.0 points, 4.1 rebounds, 1.4 steals and 1.5 three-pointers, good enough for top-90 value during that span.

news.headline: Bridges posted 19 points (9-15 FG, 1-4 3Pt), eight rebounds, two assists and one block over 37 minutes during Wednesday's 121-102 victory over Cleveland.
news.story: Bridges had his best game of the season, setting season highs in points and rebounds. His role has shrunk this year, but nights like this show he can still be a factor. With OG Anunoby (calf) sidelined, Bridges should keep getting extended minutes at the wing.

news.headline: Bridges contributed 12 points (5-8 FG, 2-3 3Pt), two rebounds, three assists and one steal across 28 minutes during Saturday's 97-96 victory over the Trail Blazers.
news.story: While Bridges' numbers from Saturday's game don't jump off the page, he came through when it mattered most for New York, drilling a buzzer-beating triple to save the day for the Knicks after they blew a 26-point lead. The 30-year-old veteran is averaging 7.8 points, 3.4 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 1.1 triples and 1.1 steals per game this season.

news.headline: Jokic totaled 18 points (6-14 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 5-5 FT), 11 rebounds, five assists, one steal and five turnovers across 33 minutes in Tuesday's 120-101 loss to the Mavs.
news.story: This was just the fifth time this season that Jokic was held to under 20 points, and the second time he's been limited to five dimes or fewer. The Mavs did a good job of mucking things up in the paint for Jokic, but he shouldn't have much trouble bouncing back Friday with a favorable matchup against the Jazz.

news.headline: Jokic recorded 37 points (14-22 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 8-10 FT), 18 rebounds, 11 assists, one steal and a block in 42 minutes during Sunday's 151-145 overtime win over the Bulls.
news.story: Jokic got off to a fast start Sunday, logging 12 points, eight rebounds and four assists in the first quarter alone. His dominance continued throughout the game, as he logged a game-high 18 rebounds and a team-high 11 assists to go along with a season-high 37 points. The star big man has now posted four triple-doubles this season.

news.headline: Jokic chipped in 26 points (10-15 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 4-4 FT), seven rebounds and 11 assists over 38 minutes during Friday's 133-124 victory over the Rockets.
news.story: Jokic was his usual efficient self, leading Denver in scoring and assists. He capped the night by setting up an Aaron Gordon alley-oop in the final seconds. The three-time MVP has been remarkably consistent, scoring at least 24 points in five straight games. He's averaging 24.2 points, 10.4 rebounds and 9.1 assists overall this season.

news.headline: Siakam (hip) will play in Monday's game against the Thunder, Justin Martinez of The Oklahoman reports.
news.story: After carrying a questionable tag ahead of both parts of this back-to-back, Siakam is suiting up Monday despite dealing with a left hip injury. Since the beginning of November, the star power forward has averaged 23.7 points, 5.1 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 1.2 steals per contest over 10 games.

news.headline: Siakam is questionable for Monday's game against Oklahoma City due to left hip injury management.

news.story: Larsson bounced back from a four-point outing in his return from illness, matching his season high in scoring. news.story: Larsson returned to the starting lineup after missing three consecutive games due to an illness, but his playing time was significantly reduced. The third-year forward averaged 12.0 points, 4.3 rebounds and 3.0 assists across his previous three appearances before the absence. His minutes will be worth monitoring as he works his way back into Miami's rotation, though his limited offensive involvement makes him a risky fantasy option in standard leagues.
